issue_title: PCA's SVD solver allocates an unused n_samples by n_samples matrix
pr_title: Avoid quadratic sample-space allocation in PCA SVD
issue_body:
### Description

The default SVD solver calls SciPy SVD on the transposed centered data with `full_matrices=True`. For a dataset with many more samples than features, this allocates the complete right-singular-vector matrix of shape `(n_samples, n_samples)`, even though PCA discards that result.

For 12,000 samples and three features, the discarded output alone is 144 million float64 values, or about 1.07 GiB. This prevents an otherwise small PCA fit from completing under a modest memory limit.

```python
import numpy as np
from mlxtend.feature_extraction import PrincipalComponentAnalysis

X = np.random.RandomState(7).normal(size=(12000, 3))
model = PrincipalComponentAnalysis(n_components=1).fit(X)
print(model.transform(X[:20]).shape)
```

### Proposed change and evidence

Request reduced SVD when the number of samples is at least the number of features. It retains the complete feature-space basis while reducing the unused right-singular-vector output from sample-square to feature-by-sample. Keep full SVD for wide data to preserve the existing complete feature-space basis and zero-eigenvalue behavior.

Two subprocess regression cases run the real public `fit` and `transform` methods with 256 MiB of additional virtual address space after imports. Unchanged master raises `_ArrayMemoryError` trying to allocate a `(12000, 12000)` float64 array in both cases. The fixed source succeeds. These are allocation regressions, not runtime or peak-RSS benchmarks.

On unchanged production source `1aee767ef57b84a8191511a08955c583b65de382`, the 13 new cases report **2 failed, 11 passed**. After the fix, the feature-extraction and base-model suites report **85 passed**.

[Successful validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/mlxtend/actions/runs/43668982683).
pr_body:
### Description

The SVD PCA solver computes the full right-singular-vector matrix of the transposed input and immediately discards it. For tall datasets this adds an unnecessary `n_samples ** 2` allocation: a 12,000-by-3 input requests about 1.07 GiB just for the discarded matrix.

Use reduced SVD when `n_samples >= n_features`, keeping the complete left-singular-vector feature basis and all public result shapes. Wide datasets continue using full SVD so their existing complete feature basis and padded eigenvalues remain unchanged. Document the allocation behavior.

### Validation

Base: `1aee767ef57b84a8191511a08955c583b65de382`. Validated source: `0c658f8b938823e6f54f2d88f11145223bdbc53e`.

- Same 13 new regression/control cases on unchanged production source: **2 failed, 11 passed**.
- Feature-extraction and base-model tests after the fix: **85 passed**.
- Two Linux subprocess regressions exercise real `fit` and `transform` on a 12,000-by-3 dataset with 256 MiB of additional address space, for both all components and one selected component. The original source fails while allocating a 1.07 GiB `(12000, 12000)` output; the fixed source succeeds.
- Tall, wide and square controls verify full feature-basis shapes, eigenvalues against an independent covariance `eigvalsh` reference, orthogonality, covariance reconstruction, transformed dimensions and unchanged inputs.
- Whitening controls verify unit covariance on retained components.
- Black, isort and Flake8 pass on both changed Python files, with a clean checkout check.
- Python 3.11.18, NumPy 2.4.0, SciPy 1.16.3, scikit-learn 1.8.0 with frozen uv dependencies on Ubuntu. The full repository suite and performance benchmarks were not run. The address-space tests are skipped on non-Linux platforms.

[Successful exact-commit validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/mlxtend/actions/runs/43668982683).

### Related work

Reviewed all-state PCA/SVD history and the actual #251, #474, #545, #565, #594, #595, #660 and #1080 diffs. All 34 pre-existing fork heads retain the full-SVD call, including the older centering and real-eigendecomposition branches. This change concerns the unused sample-space allocation and preserves their separate centering/eigensolver concerns.
